title: Zr(HSO4)4: Green, efficient and reusable catalyst for one-pot synthesis of 1,8-dioxooctahydroxanthene
author: Pourshamsian

steps.title: Prepare reaction mixture
steps.instruction: Weigh dimedone (2 mmol) and the chosen aldehyde (1 mmol) into a dry reaction vessel, then add Zr(HSO4)4 catalyst (20 mol % relative to dimedone, prepared as reported).

steps.title: Conduct catalytic condensation
steps.instruction: Stir the mixture at 110 °C under the reaction time recorded for the specific substrate (e.g., 40 min for the optimized solvent‑free condition). No additional solvent is added unless a specific solvent screening is being performed.

steps.title: Monitor reaction progress
steps.instruction: Take small aliquots periodically and analyse by TLC on 0.2 mm Merck silica‑gel GF254 plates, developing with EtOAc/diethyl ether (1:4) and visualising under 254 nm UV light.

steps.title: Quench and extract product
steps.instruction: When TLC shows complete consumption of starting materials, cool the reaction to room temperature, add an equal volume of cold water, and extract the aqueous mixture with ethyl acetate (3 × 5 mL).

steps.title: Dry and concentrate organic layer
steps.instruction: Combine the ethyl acetate extracts, dry over anhydrous MgSO4, filter off the drying agent, and evaporate the solvent under reduced pressure to afford the crude product.

steps.title: Recrystallize crude product
steps.instruction: Dissolve the crude solid in a minimal amount of 96 % ethanol, allow it to cool and crystallise, then filter and dry to obtain the pure 1,8‑dioxooctahydroxanthene derivative.

steps.title: Characterize isolated compounds
steps.instruction: Determine melting point (un‑corrected), record FT‑IR (KBr pellet) and ¹H‑NMR (CDCl₃, TMS internal standard) spectra, and compare all data with literature values to confirm structure.

steps.title: Recycle Zr(HSO4)4 catalyst
steps.instruction: After each reaction, collect the solid Zr(HSO4)4 catalyst, wash it sequentially with ethanol and water, dry it in an oven, and reuse it in a new run (up to three cycles without significant loss of activity).

steps.title: Perform antibacterial disk diffusion assay
steps.instruction: Prepare Mueller‑Hinton agar plates of 5 mm thickness, spread 50 µL of a bacterial suspension adjusted to 0.5 McFarland onto the agar surface with a sterile swab, place filter‑paper disks impregnated with the test compound at 2000 µg mL⁻¹ (3a‑3j) onto the inoculated plates, incubate 24 h at 37 °C, then measure inhibition zones with a ruler; repeat each assay three times and report the average diameter.
